title: Probing Magnetically Active Intercalant Disorder with Atomic Resolution Imaging and Spectroscopy
content: Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have attracted great interest due to their wide range of functional properties which can be tuned with changes in thickness, stacking order, and twist [1]. Introducing intercalants into the van der Waals (vdW) gap of these materials adds a rich new dimension of electrochemical, electronic and magnetic properties [2]. Of particular recent interest is the addition of magnetic intercalants, which can give rise to magnetic behavior useful for spintronics including sharp magnetization switching, chiral textures, and potentially altermagnetism [3-5]. The ability to easily manipualte these systems by altering the intercalant and host lattice structure makes these materials an ideal platform for exploring exchange interactions, magnetic correlations, and spin coupling to lattice and electronic degrees of freedom. However, the large structural configuration space, including the intercalant concentration and site occupation, as well as the composition, stacking sequence, and degree of inhomogeneity of both the intercalants and host lattice, poses a major material design challenge [6]. This complexity and the inevitable presence of disorder in real world samples makes it difficult to disentangle the connections between these structural features and the useful emergent magnetic properties realized in these materials. Here, we study 2H-NbS2, which in its pristine state hosts charge density wave and superconducting phases, intercalated with magnetic vanadium ions [7]. Introducing vanadium to the material results in a wide range of magnetic behavior associated with subtle variations in structural order and disorder extending across length scales.
